reviewer_messages: These files are disposable cache. The authoritative data is elsewhere.

reply.text: Provisional map: writing changes bare lists to a version-2 envelope; decoding rejects legacy lists, as the new test expects. The unchanged reader handles that rejection by fetching origin rows and overwriting the file: a rebuild-on-read transition. The old decoder also rejects v2, so rollback through this reader requires another refill. The deployment fixture describes an origin shared by all instances with no client limit; actual capacity and data authority remain unknown. Separately, a missing records field raises KeyError outside the reader's recovery handling, and non-list records pass through unchecked. I have recorded the validation fix for later.

reply.text:
Every read_rows call that reaches the fallback independently fetches from the configured shared origin. If every instance encounters a legacy cache at once, those requests arrive together; overlapping reads can generate several refills within one instance because nothing coalesces them.

If the origin serves the burst and writes succeed, callers receive the fetched rows and their caches become v2. If the origin slows or rejects requests, callers wait or receive exceptions. The code specifies a network timeout but no aggregate concurrency limit. It does not serve the rejected cache or retry inside that call. A fetch failure occurs before the write, so that call leaves the cache unchanged; subsequent reads can trigger more fetches unless another caller has successfully rebuilt it.

This can spread an availability problem across instances and any other consumers sharing the origin. An outage is possible, not established: origin capacity and server protections are unknown. Your disposable-cache context removes the local authoritative-data concern, but rollback can cause another refill burst because the old decoder rejects v2. The missing operational bound remains the next inquiry; no decision has been inferred from your question.
